complexity_scope.guarantee: Deterministic success under a valid distance promise; finite capped false-promise behavior with verified successful acceptance only.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: C_p depends only on fixed p after choosing the recursive implementations; independent of d, R, D, Lp and epsilon. No arithmetic or bit-complexity assertion.
complexity_scope.oracle: Exact feasible complete order-p jets, including all projected tensor information under the known affine-hull map; one nested affine jet costs one original-F query.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Explicit evaluated original-domain normal certificate (x,n,F(x)) with ||F(x)+n||<=epsilon, hence tangent residual <=epsilon.
complexity_scope.regime: All positive Lp,D,epsilon and 0<R<=D at fixed p>=2; no matching joint R/D lower bound.
complexity_scope.resource: Worst-case original-query cap, including failed trials, all descendants and evaluations; singleton <=1 query for the evaluated certificate.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Final residual solver A_{p-1} of the Algorithm 6 hierarchy, called with supplied R instead of D.

content.intended_use: Precisely state Corollary 9.1 and equation (3.6), with finite hierarchy dependencies and the public affine-hull certificate convention.

proofs.full_local_argument: Use published Proposition 5.2 as an input theorem: S0 has gamma0=2/(p+1), bS0=2. Suppose S_{j-1} has gamma_{j-1}=2/(p+2j-1) and bS_{j-1}=6j-4, where 1<=j<=p-1. The input boost parameter a_j=(p-1)gamma_{j-1}=2(p-1)/(p+2j-1) is positive and <=2. Also (3/2)a_j=3(p-1)/(p+2j-1)>=1 because j<=p-1. Finally gamma_{j-1}<=1 for p>=2 and j>=1. Thus Theorem 8.1 applies, giving Aj with gamma_j=gamma_{j-1}/(1+gamma_{j-1})=2/(p+1+2j) and bA_j=bS_{j-1}+4=6j. If j<p-1, the published residual-to-strong restart theorem gives Sj with the same gamma_j and bS_j=6j+2. This proves the induction from the stated base, using only already constructed routines, and requires exactly p-1 boosts and p-2 intermediate restart transfers. At j=p-1 the final residual interface is A_{2/(3p-1),6(p-1)}. By Definition 5.1, for any valid supplied 0<R<=D its evaluated certificate and query bound are exactly C_p(1+Q_R^(2/(3p-1)))L_A(R,epsilon)^(6(p-1)), which expands to equation (3.6). The interface includes finite prescribed interruptible caps and sound successful acceptance under false promises. These properties are preserved by the established boost and restart contracts, with every ancestor charged before each original query; hence they apply to the final call even if its supplied promise is false. No success guarantee is inferred in that case. When R=D, Q_R=Q and L_A=1+log(3+Q), so the upper expression specializes to the published diameter-only upper bound. This deduction uses no lower bound and gives no matching joint R/D dependence. For the affine-hull statement, let aff(X)=xc+U R^r with U^T U=I_r public, K={z:xc+Uz in X}, and Ftilde(z)=U^T F(xc+Uz). The map z to xc+Uz is an isometry, so diameters and initial solution distances agree. For z,v in K, <Ftilde(z)-Ftilde(v),z-v>=<F(xc+Uz)-F(xc+Uv),U(z-v)>=0. The chain rule gives D^j Ftilde(z)[v1,...,vj]=U^T D^j F(xc+Uz)[Uv1,...,Uvj]; since ||U||=||U^T||=1, the highest-derivative Lipschitz constant is at most Lp. One original full jet supplies all these tensors. Given ntilde in N_K(z), let x=xc+Uz and n=U ntilde-(I-UU^T)F(x). Every y in X has y-x=U(v-z) for v in K. Thus <n,y-x>=<ntilde,v-z><=0, proving n in N_X(x). Further, F(x)+n=UU^T F(x)+U ntilde=U(Ftilde(z)+ntilde), whose norm equals ||Ftilde(z)+ntilde|| by U^T U=I_r. The final original full F(x) was saved when simulating the evaluated reduced certificate, so the lift adds no query. At r=0, X={xc}, N_X(xc)=R^d. One query supplies F(xc), and n=-F(xc) gives an evaluated zero-residual certificate; a point-only output needs no query. This proves the claimed specialization and lift relative to the explicitly linked base, restart and boost theorems, without independently reproving their literature arguments.
map: Start with the published base strong interface.
Apply the boost exactly p-1 times, applying the published restart transfer only between boosts.
Keep R supplied in the final residual interface to obtain equation (3.6).
Use the public orthonormal affine-hull map and the saved full operator value to lift the evaluated normal certificate.

assumptions: Fixed integer p>=2, positive Lp,D,epsilon and 0<R<=D. Some VI solution zstar satisfies ||x0-zstar||<=R for the success guarantee.

Exact feasible order-p queries return complete jets (F,DF,...,D^(p-1)F). Exact projections and solving known regularized Taylor-model VIs are internal operations; lower derivatives need no separate bounds.

Use the certified published base and restart interfaces, the complete Theorem 8.1 boost and their known recursively attached constants/caps. Each call uses only an already constructed lower-level solver.

All original-F calls, failed trials, descendant calls and certificate evaluations are counted under shared interruptible ancestor caps. Successful outputs retain a genuine original-domain normal and evaluated operator value.
For a non-full-dimensional domain its affine hull and orthonormal coordinate map are public; use Appendix A.1 to reduce and lift certificates. A zero-dimensional hull uses the singleton branch.
statement.conclusion: Running A_{p-1}(F,x0,R,epsilon) returns (x,n,F(x)) with x in X, n in N_X(x), evaluated F(x), and ||F(x)+n||<=epsilon within C_p[1+(Lp R^p/epsilon)^(2/(3p-1))][1+log(2+D/R+Lp R^p/epsilon)]^(6(p-1)) original queries, equation (3.6). Under an invalid distance promise the same constructed public finite cap controls the call, and success is accepted only after verification. Taking R=D gives C_p(1+Q^alpha_p)[1+log(3+Q)]^(6(p-1)), the upper half of published Theorem 3.3. No matching joint lower dependence on independently prescribed R and D is asserted. Public affine-hull reduction preserves distance, residual norm and oracle order; an evaluated singleton certificate needs at most one query.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Finite-dimensional Euclidean R^d with induced multilinear derivative operator norm. Known nonempty compact convex X, diam(X)<=D, feasible x0. F is monotone on X, C^(p-1) on an open neighborhood and Lip(D^(p-1)F)<=Lp. N_X(x)={n:<n,u-x><=0 for all u in X}. A VI solution has -F(zstar) in N_X(zstar). Q_R=Lp R^p/epsilon, L_A(R,epsilon)=1+log(2+D/R+Q_R), alpha_p=2/(3p-1). The final solver is the acyclic A_{p-1} built from S0=AdaptiveStrong(BaseTrial), Aj=ExtrapolatedHalpern(S_{j-1}), and Sj=AdaptiveStrong(RestartTrial(Aj)) only for j<p-1.
statement.parameter_domains: d>=1; fixed integer p>=2; Lp,D,epsilon>0; 0<R<=D. No Q_R>=2 restriction is needed for the supplied-distance upper bound with its additive constant. No uniform-in-p claim.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every fixed p>=2 there exists C_p>0, independent of d and instance parameters, such that for every listed admissible public input, compatible unknown F and valid supplied R the deterministic hierarchy satisfies the stated bound. For an invalid supplied R it remains a finite capped procedure, with no guarantee of success but no unverified successful output.
